title: Quadratic Equations by Factorisation
seo_title: Quadratic Equations – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation; form quadratic equations from given roots and from word problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on quadratic equations: solving by factorisation, the difference of two squares, forming equations from roots and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: If ab = 0, then a = 0 or b = 0
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Make one side 0 first.
  • Factorise, then set each factor equal to 0.
  • Check both answers in the question; a length cannot be negative.

Examples

Example

x² + x − 12 = 0

(x + 4)(x − 3) = 0

Answer: x = −4 or x = 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by xYou lose the answer x = 0. Factorise instead.
Not making one side 0x² + x = 6 must become x² + x − 6 = 0.
Wrong signs in the roots(x + 4) = 0 gives x = −4.

items.q: A square of side x cm has a strip 5 cm wide added along one side, making a rectangle x cm by (x + 5) cm. The rectangle's area is 24 cm². Find x.
items.e: x² + 5x = 24 gives (x − 3)(x + 8) = 0. The length must be positive: x = 3.

items.q: A rectangle is x cm wide and (x + 6) cm long. Its area is 135 cm². Find x.
items.e: x(x + 6) = 135 gives x² + 6x − 135 = 0, so (x − 9)(x + 15) = 0. x = 9 or −15, but a length cannot be negative, so x = 9.

items.q: The product of two consecutive positive whole numbers is 156. What is the smaller number?
items.e: Let the numbers be x and x + 1. x² + x = 156 gives (x − 12)(x + 13) = 0. The positive answer is 12.
